method: Real Plasma Electron app (built from this repo, out/), launched with Playwright _electron at device scale factor 2, window 1440x900 CSS px, isolated empty userData, light appearance, default Plasma coral palette. Illustrative data: fictional shop (Postgres 16.2 throwaway cluster, Redis 7.2.5, OpenSearch 2.17.1). Screenshots are PNG window captures converted to WebP quality 92; dialogs cropped where noted; no editing or recolouring.

pg-workbench.webp.shows: Postgres workbench: the orders table in the data grid, sidebar listing the shop tables, row 13 selected so the Details panel shows its fields (status shown with its enum type name, order_status), connected status capsule on top.
pg-workbench.webp.capture: Full window, orders table opened by double-click in the sidebar, right sidebar shown, one cell clicked. Retaken after the enum type-name fix, from a rebuilt app and a freshly seeded throwaway database.

pg-editor.webp.shows: SQL editor with a three-statement script (revenue by country JOIN/aggregate, best sellers, status counts), run with Run all statements; result tabs Result 1-3 shown.
pg-editor.webp.capture: Script pasted into the query tab, executed via command palette 'Run all statements', Result 1 tab selected.

pg-structure.webp.shows: Structure view of the orders table with one staged change (a column comment on total) and the Preview SQL panel showing the generated BEGIN/COMMENT ON COLUMN/COMMIT.
pg-structure.webp.capture: Orders tab > Structure, typed into the Comment field of column total and blurred; change was never applied.

pg-er.webp.shows: ER diagram of the public schema (customers, products, orders, order_items, payments) with foreign-key relationships, fitted.
pg-er.webp.capture: Command palette 'Show diagram', then Fit to screen; right sidebar hidden.

pg-import.webp.shows: Import data dialog on a 48-row CSV (new_customers.csv): existing table public.customers selected, columns mapped, first rows previewed.
pg-import.webp.capture: File chosen by stubbing the native open dialog to return /tmp/new_customers.csv; Existing table > public.customers; signed_up mapped to created_at. Cropped to the dialog plus margin; import was not run.

pg-roles.webp.shows: Roles and privileges dialog with scratch role analyst selected, Table privileges tab showing SELECT grants on customers, order_items, orders, products.
pg-roles.webp.capture: Command palette 'Roles and privileges', analyst selected, Table privileges tab. Cropped to the dialog plus margin.

pg-search.webp.shows: Search in database for 'Okafor': results grouped by table (13 rows in customers, 4 rows in orders notes) with matches highlighted.
pg-search.webp.capture: Command palette 'Search in database', term typed, Enter. Cropped to the dialog plus margin.

pg-split.webp.shows: Split panes: a join query with results on the left, the orders table on the right.
pg-split.webp.capture: Query run in query-1, orders opened, command palette 'Split pane right'; right sidebar hidden.

pg-explain.webp.shows: Query plan with timing (EXPLAIN ANALYZE) for a join/aggregate: Sort > Aggregate > Hash Join > Seq Scans, with planning/execution totals.
pg-explain.webp.capture: Run dropdown > Explain > Run with ANALYZE. Cropped to the dialog plus margin.

guard-confirm.webp.shows: Safe mode confirmation 'Run this statement?' shown for DROP TABLE orders; under the default confirm-dangerous level.
guard-confirm.webp.capture: DROP TABLE orders; typed and run via palette, dialog captured and then Cancel clicked (orders still has 1,500 rows). Cropped to the dialog plus margin.

palette.webp.shows: Command palette opened with 'sh' typed: connections (shop, shop-cache, shop-search) and actions with shortcuts, over the orders table.

redis.webp.shows: Redis connection (shop-cache, Redis 7.2.5): key tree in the sidebar (cart, events, leaderboard, rate, session) and a session hash open with its fields, TTL, and Details panel.
redis.webp.capture: Connected via home card, rate/cart groups collapsed, first hash key opened, email field clicked. Full window.

opensearch.webp.shows: OpenSearch connection (shop-search, 2.17.1): products index searched with category:Outdoor AND rating:[4.5 TO *], 27 hits, one document selected in the Details panel.
opensearch.webp.capture: Index > Open search, query_string entered and run, row 3 clicked. Full window.

ai-agent.webp.shows: Workbench with the Assistant panel open over the orders grid: an earlier 'show the latest 10 orders' request whose show_table card was applied (grid sorted by placed_at, 10 rows), then 'Mark order 1042 as shipped' with a pending Change data card showing the summary, the UPDATE statement and the Preview with Safe Run / Reject buttons.
ai-agent.webp.capture: Full window, 1440x900 CSS px at 2x via Playwright _electron. Asked both questions in the Assistant panel, clicked Apply on the first card, left the second pending. Assistant replies come from a scripted local mock model (OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1) configured as the Local provider with model id llama-3.1-8b; data is a fictional shop in a throwaway Postgres cluster.

ai-memory.webp.shows: Database memory dialog for connection 'shop' with five notes, sources mixed (You / Assistant): orders.total in shop currency, test-customer email domain, ignore the archive schema, VIP = customers.vip, cancelled/refunded orders have no payment row.
ai-memory.webp.capture: Assistant panel > memory button (book icon) with notes added through the memory API as user/agent. Cropped to the dialog plus margin (x 800-2080, y 230-1570 of the 2880x1800 window). Assistant replies come from a scripted local mock model (OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1) configured as the Local provider with model id llama-3.1-8b; data is a fictional shop in a throwaway Postgres cluster.

mcp-proposal.webp.shows: An external MCP client's proposal in Plasma: the Assistant panel shows 'Claude Code wants to change data' with a pending Change data card (summary, UPDATE statement, Preview with Safe Run / Reject) over the orders grid.
mcp-proposal.webp.capture: MCP server enabled on port 47391 with access 'propose' on shop; token read from <userData>/mcp-token; real MCP session over HTTP (initialize with clientInfo 'Claude Code', then tools/call propose_change). Full window. Data is a fictional shop in a throwaway Postgres cluster.

mcp-settings.webp.shows: Settings > MCP server: enabled and listening on 127.0.0.1:47391, token hidden (bullets), Claude Code setup snippet with the token masked, per-connection access list (shop: read and propose, shop-staging: structure and read queries, shop-analytics: structure only), and Recent calls from a real Claude Code MCP session.
mcp-settings.webp.capture: Same session as mcp-proposal after declining the proposal; scrolled the settings pane slightly so every Recent calls row is visible. Token never revealed. Full window. Data is fictional.

compare.webp.shows: Result Compare tab 'shop vs shop-staging': the same orders query on two connections keyed by id, with 2 added, 2 removed, 3 changed (old value struck through) and 14 unchanged rows, unchanged rows shown.
compare.webp.capture: Command palette 'Compare results…', Side A and B both 'Run a query…' (B on shop-staging, a copy of the fictional database with a few edited rows), 'same' filter turned on. Full window. Data is fictional.

conflict.webp.shows: Edit conflict dialog 'A row changed while you were editing' on public.customers id=1: column country with Original FR, Theirs (now) DE and Yours GB, with Take theirs / Keep mine, over the customers grid in edit mode with the 'Commit failed, nothing was saved' banner.
conflict.webp.capture: Edit mode on (toolbar safety button), country cell of row 1 edited with F2 to GB, the same row changed to DE from psql, then Ctrl+S. Full window. Data is fictional (throwaway Postgres cluster).

notebook.webp.shows: Notebook dialog on the shop connection: a rendered Markdown heading and note, then two SQL cells that were run, one showing revenue per day since 5 October and one the top three countries by revenue (join of orders and customers), each with its result table under the query.
notebook.webp.capture: Command palette 'Notebook…' with a draft of one Markdown and two SQL cells (loaded from the per-connection draft), each SQL cell run with its Run button. Full window. Data is fictional (throwaway Postgres cluster).

diagnosis.webp.shows: Connection editor after Test connection on a saved connection whose database name has a typo: the plain-language problem 'Database not found' with three things to try and the step trail Find the host, Reach the port, Log in (passed) and Open the database (failed); the Database field is flagged.
diagnosis.webp.capture: Saved connection shop-staging pointing at database shop_stagng (typo) on the throwaway cluster, opened with its edit pencil, Test pressed. Full window. Data is fictional.

recovery.webp.shows: Crash recovery after a force-kill: Plasma relaunched on the same profile with the restored workspace (query-1.sql showing its unsaved multi-line SQL, query-2.sql and the customers table tab, all with unsaved markers) and the toast 'Plasma closed unexpectedly. Restored 3 tabs and 1 unsaved edit' with Discard edits and Show crash log.
recovery.webp.capture: Two SQL tabs with unsaved SQL typed in plus the customers table with one staged cell edit; waited for the recovery journal, sent SIGKILL to the Electron main process, relaunched with the same PLASMA_USER_DATA (safeStorage stub re-applied) and reloaded. Full window. Data is fictional.
